sources.title: API/BUG: support for operations with custom objects / object dtype · Issue #64107 · pandas-dev/pandas · GitHub
sources.content:
```
# operation of scalar/arr/series with string (object) other arr = np array MyObject "a" MyObject "b" ser = pd Series "1" "2" print ser + arr 0 print ser + arr print ser + pd Series arr print arr 0 + ser print arr + ser print pd Series arr + ser
```

However, this case no longer works in pandas 3.0 with the default `str` dtype. [...] For example, using the pathlib objects for which we added custom support. For string dtype, @jbrockmendel added support for auto-propagating missing values:

   ```
   >>> path/ pd Series "a" None "b" 0/ home/ a 1 NaN 2/ home/ b dtype object
   ```

   but with object dtype, it calls the element `path / None` which raises an error: [...] ```
   >>> path/ pd Series "a" None "b" dtype = object TypeError unsupported operand s for/ 'PosixPath' and 'NoneType'
   ```

Here are the following solutions you can use to fix this error: ⬇️⬇️⬇️

## TypeError unsupported operand type s for str and float

### The "TypeError unsupported operand type s for str and float" usually occurs when you try to perform an arithmetic…

itsourcecode.com

## Conclusion

By implementing the solutions provided in the aforementioned link, you can resolve the error you are encountering. [...] In addition to that, the error message indicates that you are trying to use a mathematical operator (such as +, -, \, or /) between a string and a float (a decimal number).

Unfortunately, these two data types cannot be used together in mathematical operations.

For example:

```
income = 150000.00profit = 10000.00print("Your total income this year is " + salary + bonus + ".") "Your total income this year is ""."
```

As a result, it will throw an error message.
